title: Field Office architecture portfolio
audience: Cultural institutions and residential clients selecting an architecture studio
scenario: Field Office is a small architecture practice focused on adaptive reuse and materially restrained additions.
task: Build a portfolio homepage that foregrounds project thinking, makes the studio's approach legible, and supports project inquiries.

sections: Navigation with Work, Practice, Notes, Contact, and Project inquiry
Introductory statement about adaptive reuse and careful additions
Featured project: Loom House, Hamilton, 2025, residential conversion
Project index including Archive Hall, Moss Courtyard, Northline Workshop, and Quarry Rooms
Practice statement covering reuse, daylight, and durable material choices
Selected note titled What the existing wall already knows

requirements: Represent project names, locations, years, and types as accessible text
Keep the featured project and project index semantically distinct
Provide an explicit project inquiry action
Use a logical heading hierarchy suitable for a portfolio index
Make the content structure resilient when imagery is unavailable
constraints: Do not fabricate awards, press coverage, client names, or project dimensions
Do not use remote photography or external fonts
Do not turn the project index into non-semantic clickable containers
Avoid generic agency phrases such as award-winning or world-class
evaluation_focus: Editorial hierarchy across featured work, index, practice, and notes
Project metadata clarity without visual evidence
Specific studio voice and inquiry path
